title: Understanding the request
purpose: Before any work, a fast open model reads your message with the last few exchanges and says what you want now, what kind of task it is, what you expect at the end, whether you are unhappy with the last answer, and what would be a misunderstanding. The agent works from that, and you see it as "Understood: …".
handles: you run it and give the link
where to download here? (about the Flutter page you pasted)
chainNote: Open models first: gpt-oss and Qwen on Groq (about a second), then Nemotron on NVIDIA (2 to 8 seconds). After 10 seconds, or on any error, the older keyword rules decide.

effort.note: One JSON answer; skipped for small talk, "continue" and a first plain question.

tools.note: None: it only reads the conversation.

context: The names and first lines of pasted text
approach: Resolve "it", "this" and "here" from the conversation
A short or angry message continues the previous goal: do it, do not tell the user to
A path to a zip or installer means install from it and carry on
Pick the kind of work, which picks the method, the tier, references and file search
Ask one question only when nothing sensible can be done without it
checks: A deck, Word file or PDF deliverable is always documents, whatever the model says
Every path and URL in the message is kept

tokens.note: Measured on 14 real and everyday requests: 14 of 14 right on Groq and on NVIDIA.

strengths: Fixes the misreads of real chats: "here" with an attachment, "business model", "you run it"
Fails safe: without it, nothing changes
weaknesses: Adds about a second before the work starts
A provider at its rate limit can make it time out, and the keyword rules decide
improvements: Learn from complaints which understandings were wrong, and add them to the evaluation set

title: Small talk and general questions
purpose: Greetings, thanks, and questions about the world rather than the project: answered at once from knowledge, with no project context.
handles: What is the difference between REST and GraphQL?
How does a hash map work?
chainNote: Fast models first. Your own Claude or OpenAI key is only used first when no free key is active; otherwise it waits at the end of the chain.

effort.note: Answered in a single request; the conversation resent is cut to the last 2 exchanges.

tools.note: None: nothing to read or change.

context: A short system prompt of about 150 tokens
approach: Recognise small talk or a general question (no project words in it)
Reply in 1 to 3 warm sentences, or a structured answer with a comparison and an example for a question
Never claim to have looked at files
checks: None needed: nothing is changed
strengths: About 90% cheaper than running the full agent
Warm and natural, matches your tone and language
weaknesses: Cannot see your project, so it answers in general terms
A question that is secretly about the project can be misjudged
improvements: Offer to run the full agent when the answer mentions "your project"

title: Fyx: chores with no model
purpose: Everyday chores run by the extension itself: git, zip, installing packages, starting a dev server, creating or moving files.
chainNote: No model, no key, no tokens. Anything it cannot do is handed to the Auto chain.

effort.note: A fixed plan per chore; every command still asks permission.

context: Which tools your project has (package manager, git)
approach: Match the request to a known chore or a chore learned from you or from other users (approved)
Fill in names from your request
Run the commands and report
checks: Exit codes of each command

tokens.note: It runs in seconds and uses no tokens.

strengths: Instant and free; saves your keys for real work
Learns new chores from corrections
weaknesses: Only chores it knows; unusual phrasing falls through to a model
improvements: More chores from the shared Fyx patterns you approve on the Learning page

title: Run and preview
purpose: Starts your project so you can see it, installing a missing toolchain from a file you supplied, and gives you the live link.
handles: run my Flutter app and give me the localhost link
install Flutter from this zip and run it

effort.note: Long installs and first builds run in the background and are checked on.

tools.note: All tools; run_command with background=true and the process tool do the work.

context: No design references and no code search: they do not help here
approach: Find how the project starts
"Not on PATH" is not "not installed": look in the usual places first
Install from your zip into a folder outside OneDrive and the project, in the background
Start it in the background, read the address it prints, open it with fetch_url
Give the link and how to stop it; change nothing else
checks: The editor opens the link itself before the agent may give it, and loads it in a hidden browser; browser errors send it back
After any code change, the compile check of the stack (Flutter analyze, errors only) must pass after the last edit
An edit that would unbalance the brackets of a code file is refused before it is written
A server is not started on a port that is taken: its own process is named, or a free port is offered when another program holds it
At most 3 starts of the same app per task, then an honest report instead of more guesses
Commands written for another shell (%USERPROFILE%, cmd /c, taskkill /PID, PowerShell in double quotes) are fixed or refused before they run

tokens.note: A first Flutter web build takes minutes, not tokens.

strengths: Does the work instead of handing you commands
Reports the real address the server printed
weaknesses: Steps that need administrator rights or a device still need you
improvements: Remember where each toolchain was installed, per computer

title: Quick tasks
purpose: Small, clear requests: a one-line fix, a rename, a short edit, running one command.
handles: add a null check in cart.js
chainNote: Groq first (answers in a second or two), then Gemini lite, NVIDIA, Mistral. Your own Claude or OpenAI key is only used first when no free key is active; otherwise it waits at the end of the chain.

effort.note: Reasoning kept low for speed; no plan, no exploring.

tools.note: Read, search, edit and one command; nothing else is offered, to save tokens.

context: The 4 most likely files named up front
approach: Act at once with the fewest calls
Edit by line numbers
Run the project check if it has one
checks: The editor's errors on the changed file come back with each edit
strengths: Fast: Groq replies in about a second
Cheap
weaknesses: Small context per request on Groq: a large file moves the task to another provider
improvements: Learned order from real outcomes once a provider has 20+ tasks

title: Explaining a project
purpose: Understanding code: how something works, what a project is, where a feature lives. Changes nothing.
handles: where is the order total calculated?
chainNote: Same fast chain; the project overview and main files travel with the request, so it usually answers in one step.

effort.note: Answers from the code already supplied.

context: The 4 most-used code files (up to 12,000 characters)
A code map when the project is large
approach: Answer from the code, not from general knowledge: read the relevant files and cite them as path:line.

Read the main files together in one reply (the ones the overview or code map points to, usually 2-5) before answering, so every claim is checked. Never write "not shown": read the file or leave it out, and do not repeat what a README says about files you have not opened.
Lead with the direct answer in a sentence or two, then the detail.
Change nothing unless the user asks.
checks: The answer cites the files it came from.
No files were changed.

tokens.note: Measured: 3,648 tokens in 1 step (before: 9,900 in 5 steps).

strengths: Cites path:line for each claim
One step on small and medium projects
weaknesses: Very large projects still need several reads
Binary and generated files are skipped
improvements: Keep a cached project summary so repeat questions cost less

title: Building new things
purpose: A new site, app, API or feature, from nothing: structure, files, running and checking it.
handles: build a playground site with a get started button
create a REST API for tasks
chainNote: Strongest first: Gemini's 1M-token context carries multi-file work, then NVIDIA Nemotron Ultra, Mistral. OpenRouter's free router last. Your own Claude or OpenAI key is only used first when no free key is active; otherwise it waits at the end of the chain.

effort.note: Plans with a todo list, writes whole files, then checks them.

tools.note: Everything except project search (nothing to search yet).

context: The matching playbook (web, python, mobile, .NET, documents...)
A proven structure for the domain (landing, dashboard, store, auth...)
A design reference for anything with a screen
approach: Understand the project before adding to it: its structure, the patterns it already uses for similar things, and how it is run and tested.
Plan the change as concrete steps with todo_write, ending with how it will be verified.
Build it end to end — data, logic, interface, wiring — rather than a front with nothing behind it. Never leave a placeholder that looks finished.
Follow the project’s existing conventions for naming, structure and error handling.
Handle the failure cases a real user will hit: empty input, no network, a slow response, a missing permission.
Run it, and the project’s checks, before finishing.
checks: It works end to end, with nothing faked.
The project’s own checks pass.
The report says how to use it and what is left to do.
Web pages load in a hidden browser: errors, cut-off layout, invisible content
Build, type check and tests when the project has them

tokens.note: Measured: a landing page 56K tokens; it writes real files, so it costs more than a fix.

strengths: Starts from how strong projects are built, not a blank page
Cannot finish on a broken build
weaknesses: Free models vary in craft; the design reference lifts the floor, not the ceiling
Long builds can hit a free daily limit mid-way (it switches keys, but not always enough)
improvements: Compare screenshots with the design reference

title: Changing existing code
purpose: Features and edits in a project that already exists: add, update, wire up, extend.
handles: add pagination to the orders list
connect the form to the API
chainNote: Strongest first, with the code map of the project up front.
context: The playbook for the project's stack
A code map: the most-used files and what they define
Your lessons and approved shared lessons
approach: Find the relevant code with search, not folder by folder
Read only what is needed
Edit by line, then run the project's own checks
Fix what the editor reports on each edit
checks: The project's tests, type check or build must pass after the last edit before it can finish

tokens.note: Depends on how many files it must read.

strengths: Edits by line number avoid most "text not found" retries
Reads only the files that matter
weaknesses: Projects with no tests can only be checked by build or page load
improvements: Remember which files each feature touches between tasks

title: Debugging
purpose: Something is broken: reproduce it, find the cause, fix it, prove it.
handles: fix the bug: total() returns NaN for an empty cart
chainNote: Strongest first. When the same error repeats, the next steps go to the strongest model available with an instruction to fix the root cause.

effort.note: After an error repeats twice (even with other steps between), 2 steps run on the strongest model; after 5 repeats it stops instead of burning tokens.

context: The error text and likely files
approach: Reproduce it first. Find or write the smallest command, test or input that shows the failure, and run it. If you cannot reproduce it, say so and ask for what you need — do not guess at a fix.
Find the cause, not the symptom. Read the code path the failure goes through and state in one sentence why it happens before changing anything.
Make the smallest change that removes the cause. Do not refactor, rename or restyle anything else on the way.
Add a test that failed before the fix and passes after it, where the project has tests.
Run the reproduction again and show it passing.
checks: The reproduction was run before and after, and now passes.
The cause is stated in one sentence in the report.
Nothing unrelated to the bug was changed.

tokens.note: Measured 32K to 46K on the cart bug.

strengths: Reproduces first and proves the fix
Escalates to the strongest model on a stubborn error
weaknesses: If the bug cannot be reproduced it says so and asks, which costs a turn
improvements: Run the failing test automatically as the very first step

title: Interface design
purpose: How something looks: layout, spacing, type, colour, responsiveness, accessibility.
chainNote: Strongest first. A design reference (downloaded library first, then 8 built-in styles) travels with the request.

effort.note: Design system first, then screens, then the page check.

tools.note: All tools, plus find_image for real photos.

context: One design reference with tokens (colours, type, spacing)
Domain structure for the kind of site
approach: Read the existing design first: the component library, tokens or CSS variables, spacing scale and one or two similar screens. Match them; do not introduce a second style.
Reuse existing components before writing new ones.
Build for small screens as well as large: check the layout at phone width, and that nothing overflows horizontally.
Keep it accessible: real buttons and labels, visible focus, text contrast that passes, images with alt text.
Where the project can run, start it and check the result rather than assuming it looks right.
checks: Uses the project’s existing components and tokens.
Checked at phone width with no horizontal overflow.
Interactive elements are reachable by keyboard and labelled.
The page check scrolls the page and fails on text that never becomes visible

tokens.note: Writes CSS and markup; largest outputs of any role.

strengths: Starts from a real visual system
Checks phone width and accessibility
weaknesses: No visual judgement of the final picture yet: it checks structure, not taste
improvements: Screenshot comparison against the reference for a second opinion

title: Refactoring
approach: The rule: behaviour does not change. If a change would alter what the program does, stop and ask.
Run the existing tests before touching anything, and record which pass. If there are none for this code, write a few that pin down current behaviour first.
Move in small steps, running the tests after each one. Never combine a refactor with a feature or a fix.
Update every caller of anything renamed or moved — search the whole project, not just the open file.
checks: The same tests pass after as before.
No behaviour changed, or every change was agreed with the user.
No caller was left pointing at an old name.

tokens.note: Reads a lot before changing anything.

strengths: Behaviour is checked by tests before and after
weaknesses: Without tests it can only check that the build still passes
improvements: Offer to write characterisation tests first when none exist

title: Data and machine learning
chainNote: Strongest first. Training runs are smoke-tested on a tiny sample, never run in full.

effort.note: Baseline first, then the real model, with real metrics.

context: Shapes and a few rows, never whole datasets
approach: Make it reproducible: fix random seeds, pin versions, and never train or evaluate on data the model has already seen.
Look at the data before modelling it: shape, types, missing values, class balance. Say what you found.
Start with the simplest baseline and report its score, so any improvement means something.
Keep training small enough to run here. Anything needing a GPU or hours of compute: write it, test it on a tiny sample, and say what the full run needs.
Report metrics on a held-out set, with the number, not a description of it.
checks: Seeds are fixed and the split is held out.
A baseline score and the new score are both reported.
It was run end to end, at least on a small sample.

tokens.note: Varies with how much exploration the dataset needs.

strengths: Fixed seeds, held-out data and a baseline by default
weaknesses: Cannot judge model quality on your real data without running it
improvements: A reusable experiment template (config, metrics, saved pipeline)

title: Decks, documents and PDFs
purpose: PowerPoint, Word and PDF files built by script from an outline, designed, then rendered and reviewed page by page until they are ready.
handles: make a 12-slide deck on Nepal floods
create a presentation on the business model of a hybrid store
write a project report as a PDF

effort.note: One build script, then check_document and fixes, at most three rounds.

tools.note: Build tools plus make_deck (decks from an outline, built with PptxGenJS), find_image (real photos with credits) and check_document (file checks and a visual review).

context: The documents playbook (outline first, varied layouts, palette, grid, headline rules)
Library docs for python-pptx and python-docx on demand
approach: Decks: the agent writes only the outline (a headline, points and a layout per slide); make_deck lays it out with tested designs and native, editable charts

Gamma-style layouts: pictures filling one side, icon cards (85 Lucide icons drawn as native shapes), pill tags, steps, tables, galleries, timelines, callouts and a closing statement; 8 themes with their own font pairs; figures only with a source
Real photos from Wikimedia Commons or a labelled frame
Render the pages (its PDF copy, PowerPoint, Word or LibreOffice) and have Gemini review them as a reader would
Fix what the review lists in the script and rebuild, as PPTAgent does
checks: Empty placeholders, content off the slide, tiny or overflowing text, empty or crowded slides, blank paragraphs, blank PDF pages
A visual review of each page: cut-off text, contrast, walls of text, weak pictures, inconsistent design, a weak story, with scores for content, design and coherence

tokens.note: Each visual review is about 5K Gemini tokens (an 8-slide deck: 4.6K in, 0.2K out, 9 seconds).

strengths: Never leaves a blank template box
Photos come with their credits
Sees the deck as you will, not just its XML
weaknesses: Charts are drawn with matplotlib, so they are pictures, not editable charts
The visual review needs a Gemini key and PowerPoint, Word or LibreOffice (or the PDF copy)
improvements: Start from your own template when you attach one

title: Corrections
purpose: You point at what is wrong (often with a screenshot); each point is fixed and verified separately.
handles: the button is still blue, and the title is cut off

effort.note: Each point becomes its own item.

context: A correction brief that numbers your points
Evidence read from your screenshot or notes
approach: Number each point
Smallest change per point
Verify each one
End with what was wrong, what changed, how it was checked
checks: Each point verified separately

tokens.note: Usually fewer steps than the original task.

strengths: Saves a lesson from each correction (and shares it if you chose to)
weaknesses: A vague correction ("make it better") gives it little to verify
improvements: Ask one clarifying question when a point cannot be verified

title: Attachment reader: documents and screenshots
purpose: Turns files you attach into text the agent can use: documents are read on your computer; screenshots go to a vision model only when needed.
chainNote: Documents and text in screenshots are read locally with no model. A vision model is asked only when an image has little text or when layout and colour matter; only keys whose model can see images are used.

effort.note: Local reading first; one vision call at most per image.

context: Long documents are summarised and saved in .freeagentcoder/attachments/
approach: Detect the real format from the bytes, not the extension
Read locally: PDF, Word, PowerPoint, Excel, OpenDocument, EPUB, ZIP, e-mail, old Office files, text and code
OCR images on this computer
Ask a vision model only when needed
checks: Reports plainly when a file could not be read, never describes an image it was not shown
strengths: Private: documents are read on your computer
20+ formats
weaknesses: Scanned pages with no text layer need a vision model (Gemini, Mistral, OpenAI or Anthropic key)

title: Scanned PDF reader
purpose: PDFs with no text layer (scans): read natively by a model that accepts PDFs.
chainNote: Only Gemini reads PDFs natively; without a Gemini key it says so instead of guessing.
approach: Try the text layer locally
Only if empty, send the PDF to Gemini
checks: Page counts compared with what came back
strengths: Handles scans a local reader cannot
weaknesses: Needs a Gemini key
improvements: Local OCR for scanned PDFs on machines without a Gemini key

title: Lesson writer
purpose: After a correction, writes the short general rule to remember (and to share, if you chose to).
chainNote: The quick-task chain: a lesson is a few sentences.
approach: Write 1 to 2 general rules
Strip names, paths and secrets
Skip if it duplicates an existing lesson
checks: A rule is only shared if it passes the privacy filter
strengths: Cheap, and runs in the background
weaknesses: A lesson is only as good as the correction
